newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge settles water issue at Morenci.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge settles water issue at Morenci.

text.p: Phelps Dodge has reached a tentative settlement with the San Carlos Apache Tribe on the Black River pump station, a water source for the company's Morenci copper mine in Arizona which allows the company to continue to use the water.
The water is necessary to operate the mine's concentrator and its solvent-extraction electrowinning plant. The mine produces 225,000 tonnes of copper per year.

The tribe intially gave Phelps Dodge until the end of July to stop using the reservation for water transportation but the company reached an agreement with the tribe through the Department of Interior's Bureau of Reclamation, in which the bureau will train the tribal members to operate the pump station and lease the water to the company, according to Tim Snider, president of Phelps Dodge Morenci Corp, a subsidiary of Phelps Dodge.
The Bureau assumed control of the pump station in late July and will maintain control until the tribal members can operate it efficiently or until July 1998, whichever comes first.
Under the terms of the settlement, Phelps Dodge will pay the tribe $25,000 a month plus a lease rate to be negotiated between the company and tribe.
"What we hope is that we can become business partners with the San Carlos Apache tribe," Snider said. "We pay them to run an efficient pump station. If they don't, we don't pay them."
Black River accounts for half of Morenci's water needs and the company has made contingency plans in the event that the Black River pump station is not efficient, he said.

The company uses Eagle Creek, which is partially located on the reservation, to transport water from Black River to the Morenci complex. The company has agreed to pay an additional $5,000 a month for the right to use Eagle Creek.
The agreement doesn't waive any future action to be taken by the tribe against Phelps Dodge.
The tribe's attorney Joe Sparks did not return repeated phone calls requesting comment.
